final_recommendation: The room converged on a forced merger with UBS as the only viable path, to be announced Sunday evening before Asian markets open. This requires government loss guarantees (CHF 9-12bn), SNB liquidity backstop (CHF 100bn+), AT1 write-down to zero, and acceptance of litigation risk.
minority_objections: Nationalization presented as fallback if UBS refuses, but characterized as creating sovereign credit concerns with no clear exit strategy
key_conflicts: AT1 bondholders vs regulators: write-down while equity retains value inverts normal capital structure hierarchy and invites litigation
UBS shareholders vs government: UBS demands extraordinary guarantees and indemnities while government needs private-sector solution narrative
Federal Council vs taxpayers: fiscal guarantees are politically toxic but failure is existential
FINMA vs AT1 market precedent: write-down would devastate European AT1 market (€200bn+ outstanding)
key_concessions: Government gives CHF 9-12bn loss guarantee on specific CS asset pools plus competition law waiver; gets UBS acquisition and private-sector solution narrative
SNB gives CHF 100-200bn liquidity line accepting balance sheet expansion; gets government fiscal guarantee backing so SNB not absorbing credit risk

UBS gives agreement to acquire at government price on short timeline; gets government loss-sharing on CHF 25-40bn riskiest assets, SNB liquidity, regulatory capital relief, competition waiver, legal liability shield
FINMA gives regulatory forbearance on UBS capital ratios and fast-track approvals; gets UBS commitment and CS management departure
CS management gives board resignation and acceptance of nominal sale price; gets legal indemnification and severance packages
red_lines: Decision must be final and announced by Sunday 18:00 CET before Asian markets open Monday 01:00 CET
UBS requires government loss guarantee (CHF 9-12bn ceiling) and SNB liquidity backstop as non-negotiable conditions to proceed
Switzerland cannot afford G-SIB failure - systemic risk to Swiss financial center characterized as existential
AT1 write-down decision must be made by Sunday 12:00 to include in announcement despite litigation risk
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Cross-border regulatory coordination with ECB, Fed, BoE dismissed as 'procedural' with weekend hotlines, assuming peers will accept fait accompli
UBS shareholder revolt characterized as manageable secondary risk despite dilutive acquisition
Political backlash from left and right framed as manageable by emphasizing job losses prevented
Employee integration risk and mass layoffs mentioned but deferred as Tier 2/3 decisions
downstream_risk_variables: Whether UBS board actually approves under proposed terms (40-50% probability of refusal cited)
Whether weekend deposit flight accelerates beyond bridgeable threshold (70-80% probability if no Sunday announcement)
Whether AT1 bondholders obtain legal injunction (30-40% probability)
Whether top 100 client outreach successfully prevents pre-positioned Monday redemptions
Whether European AT1 market experiences contagion from precedent-setting write-down
Whether SNB can unwind CHF 100-200bn support within committed 24-month timeframe
uncertainty_notes: UBS acceptance remains highly uncertain (40-50% refusal probability without extraordinary support). Weekend deposit flight trajectory unknown but critical - if institutional clients pre-position Monday redemptions, liquidity gap becomes unbridgeable. AT1 legal treatment is most contentious unresolved issue with three options presented but no final decision recorded. Cross-border regulatory reactions assumed manageable but not confirmed. Actual scope of government loss guarantee depends on Saturday UBS due diligence not yet conducted.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Standalone stabilization explicitly rejected as 'not credible given structural governance failures'; liquidity alone cannot restore confidence after multi-year trust erosion and Saudi National Bank refusal
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Forced merger with UBS is the primary recommendation and dominant decision path; concrete weekend negotiation steps, pricing (CHF 0.50/share), and timeline through Sunday 18:00 announcement all specified
marker_evidence.government_support: Government loss guarantee (CHF 9-12bn) and SNB liquidity backstop (CHF 100bn+) are non-negotiable UBS conditions and binding constraints on the deal structure; characterized as decisive factors
marker_evidence.client_flight: Weekend deposit flight (70-80% probability without Sunday announcement) identified as decisive risk that could make liquidity gap 'unbridgeable even with SNB support'; drives Sunday 18:00 hard deadline and top-100 client outreach requirement
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down to zero is recommended decision (Option 1) with Sunday 12:00 deadline; drives legal opinion requirement and is framed as necessary for 'clean balance sheet for UBS' despite litigation risk
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 vs equity hierarchy conflict identified as 'most legally and financially contentious issue'; write-down while equity retains value characterized as inverting capital structure norms and fundamental dispute requiring explicit decision
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 legal injunction risk (30-40% probability) and broader litigation acknowledged and mitigation strategies proposed (legal opinions, regulatory coordination), but decision is to proceed with write-down accepting litigation as 'secondary to systemic stability'
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Sunday 18:00 CET hard deadline before Asian Monday 01:00 open drives entire critical path timeline; Tier 1 decisions must be final by then; 'every hour of delay past Sunday 18:00 exponentially increases risk of catastrophic failure'
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Allowing Monday open without resolution characterized as resulting in 'uncontrolled bank run, contagion to other Swiss banks, Swiss Franc crisis, potential G-SIB disorderly failure'; drives Sunday evening announcement requirement
